title: Paxi (Paxos/EPaxos) & HotStuff — node-level view (no native metrics)
description: HONESTY FIRST: neither Paxi nor asonnino/HotStuff exposes server metrics — for these systems the server-side account is node_exporter plus parsed logs (methodology §2 says so in every figure). This dashboard is therefore RESOURCES + the harness timeline, and the per-run logs/ directory is the protocol evidence.

panels.title: How to read Paxi and HotStuff runs (logs are the metrics)

options.content:
**Paxi baseline (corpus anchor: Ailijiang et al. SIGMOD'19 — in-memory commits, so NO disk-write signal is EXPECTED; that asymmetry vs etcd/Kafka is D6, documented not equalized):** PAXOS = single leader, so node1's CPU and NIC-tx sit visibly above the followers (it fans out Phase-2a to both); EPAXOS = leaderless round-robin, so all three lines should be roughly SYMMETRIC — visible asymmetry in an EPaxos run means the round-robin is not reaching all replicas (check endpoints). The D7 conflict sweep (c=2/10%) should show CPU rising with c on EPaxos (dependency tracking) — the fast-path effect the thesis measures.

**Paxi leader_kill = THE WEDGE (F26, preregistered):** commits STOP and never recover; the dead node's line drops, the survivors idle. That flatline is the honest result (no failure detector in stock paxi) — contrast with etcd's sub-second recovery. `failover_ms: null` is CORRECT.

**HotStuff baseline (corpus anchor: Yin et al. '19 — linear message complexity; published runs used 16-vCPU nodes, ours are larger-class ccx per D9 but still below that: absolute numbers are OURS, only direction/order compares):** all four nodes' CPU/NIC roughly symmetric (rotating leadership); the client's target node slightly busier (it batches the client's txs). Result = summary.txt + logs/ in the run dir; if `rate too high` appears in client.log, the offered rate exceeded the client — lower it, the cell is not evidence of a system ceiling.

**Suspect signs (both):** any disk-write surge on a Paxi node = something else is writing on that VM (stationarity violation, gate 4); one HotStuff node at zero CPU while others commit = it never joined (committee mismatch — regenerate, check `docker logs thesis-hs<i>` for 'panic').
